back: awareness → obedience → damage → recovery → irrecoverability. Two links (awareness, single-pass obedience drop) did not reproduce at the cheap tier.
The models do not flag the wrong-location repair instruction as wrong (0/6). Kimi K2.5 reads ~25% vs the paper's 63%. Diagnosis: 'blindness, not blind obedience.'

front: 'Blindness, not blind obedience' — what it means
back: The cheap models are not defying a rule they see; they never register the bad instruction as wrong. So the failure is perception, not obedience.
deepseek d=+0.04 [−0.022,+0.103], qwen d=+0.036 [−0.034,+0.106] — both CIs cross zero, neither near the pre-committed 10-pt bar. A single bad pass does not measurably drop the pass rate.

front: Why is the obedience drop measured on matched pairs?
back: Same problem before and after the bad instruction (paired/Newcombe). Matching removes per-problem difficulty as a confound, so the CI reflects the instruction's effect.

front: Why was ghost-patch's M4 gate underpowered — and how handled?
back: The milestone funnel left 16 or fewer clean pairs per model. It was *pre-declared* underpowered and run descriptively, with the label kept on it — never claimed to resolve irrecoverability.

No — the read is the failure needs a stronger model (awareness is absent at the cheap tier) or the iterative-plus-sabotage regime, not a single pass. Structure reproduced where powered; nulls reported where not. Ran for $1.42.
